title: Consolidations and Variable Interest Entities - ASC 810

consolidation_overview.when_required: Parent has controlling financial interest in subsidiary

two_models.when: Control through majority voting interest (>50% of voting stock)

voting_interest_model.control_test: Parent owns >50% of subsidiary's voting stock
consolidation_procedure: Combine 100% of parent and subsidiary assets, liabilities, revenues, expenses
Recognize noncontrolling interest (NCI) for portion not owned by parent

key_eliminations.entry:
DR Common Stock (sub)
DR APIC (sub)
DR Retained Earnings (sub)
   CR Investment in Sub
   CR NCI

DR Sales (selling entity)
   CR COGS (buying entity)

DR Accounts Payable
   CR Accounts Receivable

DR COGS (or Retained Earnings)
   CR Inventory

key_eliminations.elimination: Eliminate dividend income and dividends paid
key_eliminations.entry:
DR Dividend Income
   CR Dividends Paid

noncontrolling_interest.definition: Equity in subsidiary not attributable to parent (minority interest)
noncontrolling_interest.income_statement: Consolidated NI includes 100% of subsidiary income, then subtract NCI's share to arrive at NI attributable to parent
noncontrolling_interest.balance_sheet: NCI reported in equity section (separately from parent shareholders' equity)
noncontrolling_interest.calculation: Beginning NCI + NCI share of subsidiary income - NCI share of subsidiary dividends = Ending NCI

vie_criteria: Insufficient equity investment at risk (typically <10% of assets)
Equity holders not exposed to losses/returns proportionate to ownership
pb_criteria_both_required: Power to direct activities that most significantly impact VIE's economic performance
Obligation to absorb losses or right to receive benefits that could be significant to VIE
examples: Joint ventures with unusual risk/reward structures

date_of_acquisition.measurement: Subsidiary's identifiable assets and liabilities at fair value
date_of_acquisition.goodwill: Goodwill = Consideration paid + FV of NCI - FV of identifiable net assets
date_of_acquisition.entry:
DR Assets (at FV)
DR Goodwill
   CR Liabilities (at FV)

   CR NCI (at FV)

acquisition_method.subsequent_periods: Amortize fair value adjustments (e.g., depreciation on FV step-up), test goodwill for impairment

facts: Parent owns 80% of Sub (acquired at book value = FV)
Year 1: Sub has NI of $50K, pays dividends of $20K
Intercompany sales: Parent sold inventory to Sub for $100K (cost $80K). Sub still holds all inventory at year-end.

DR Common Stock (Sub) $100,000
DR Retained Earnings (Sub) $200,000
   CR Investment in Sub $240,000
   CR NCI $60,000

cpa_exam_strategies.consolidation_trigger: >50% ownership = consolidate (voting model) OR primary beneficiary of VIE = consolidate
cpa_exam_strategies.elimination_entries: Most tested: Eliminate investment vs. equity, intercompany sales, intercompany inventory profits, intercompany dividends
cpa_exam_strategies.nci_calculation: NCI % × Sub's equity. Update for NCI's share of income and dividends.
cpa_exam_strategies.vie_identification: Look for: insufficient equity, special structure, disproportionate risk/reward. Test for power + economics = primary beneficiary.
cpa_exam_strategies.common_mistakes: Forgetting to eliminate intercompany profit, incorrect NCI calculation, not eliminating 100% of intercompany transactions

key_points: Consolidate if >50% voting control OR primary beneficiary of VIE
Combine 100% of parent and sub, eliminate intercompany items, recognize NCI
NCI = Minority % × Sub's equity, adjusted for their share of income and dividends
VIE: Primary beneficiary has power AND economics - must consolidate
Key eliminations: Investment vs. equity, intercompany sales/COGS, intercompany inventory profits, intercompany AR/AP, intercompany dividends
Goodwill = Consideration + FV of NCI - FV of identifiable net assets
